claims.evidence: Read every claim and citation in the thirteen pages. HEAD-checked all 25 distinct external URLs in the seven 22 October files: 20 returned 200 or 202; PubMed (5 URLs) and drinkag1.com returned 429 rate limiting with correct IDs and paths; the arbitrationlaw.com CAS award PDF returned 404 and was replaced by the Wayback Machine copy of the CAS jurisprudence PDF, which I opened and confirmed is the award of 6 February 2012 in CAS 2011/A/2384 and 2386, and whose facts section supports the sample, laboratory, concentration and procedural claims. Two claim-source strings that referenced paragraph numbers the award does not use now cite its facts section. The 12 October files cite PubMed records whose IDs match the papers named. Race facts and times match the cited Cyclingnews reports.

editorial.evidence: Each of the thirteen pages answers a stated reader question with a specific answer (see release.json sections). British English applied: seven sponsor paragraphs changed from "program" to "programme"; the only other US spelling is inside a quoted paper title. Banned-term grep returned only that paper title. Fixed the "and and" typo and the stale "last weekend" phrase. Related slugs and in-body internal links in all thirteen files resolve to existing content files. No empty examples or invented training prescriptions; the strength pieces state the low-certainty evidence and Roadman's no-heavy-barbell position explicitly.

offers.evidence: No new products, prices, membership inclusions or testimonials. CTAs are the existing Not Done Yet application link, the free Skool community link and the sponsor boilerplate (TrainingPeaks ROADMAN code, AG1, Vittoria, POC, Bikmo, Voy) already used on earlier episodes. Training camps pages and other dirty files in the main checkout are not part of this tree.
